clue.text: Chance acquaintance is no Good Samaritan

blocks.note: first meaning: someone you meet only by happening to walk past
second meaning: in the parable, those who were no Samaritan walked past on the other side

explanation.surface: A warning that someone you meet by chance will not necessarily help you.
explanation.walkthrough: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, a priest and a Levite saw the injured man and passed by on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who merely walks past is a casual stranger, and is exactly what the priest and Levite in the parable were.

clue.text: Stout glass dashed against the wall

blocks.note: first meaning: thick lenses are called by this name, as in the spectacles
second meaning: the small stones in the rough wall rendering named after them, flung against the wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer and 'glass' a pint; pebble glasses are very thick spectacles, and pebbledash is a rendering of small stones thrown onto a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick lens glass and the small stones thrown into wall rendering both take this word for a smooth stone.

clue.text: Feed leaders of school in lunch period

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: first letters of school, in and lunch
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to give the senior pupils something to eat at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its initial letter is needed too.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented green fodder stored for cattle in winter is animal feed, the noun sense.

clue.text: He bills me for making new dress up

indicators.note: making something new from these letters means arranging them afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor complains that he charges the speaker for altering a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new dress' reads as a garment, but 'new' works on the letters before it and 'dress up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate or add ornamental detail to something is to make it look finer.

clue.text: Family dishonoured, but showing signs of fight?

blocks.note: blood means family or lineage
a stained reputation is dishonoured

explanation.surface: A family has been disgraced, though it looks as if it put up a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks of gore are left on someone after a violent brawl, which the question mark flags as an example.

clue.text: Pre-Raphaelite dance

blocks.note: first meaning: William ..., designer and poet associated with the Pre-Raphaelite circle
second meaning: the English folk dance performed with bells and sticks

explanation.walkthrough: A morris dance is a traditional English folk dance with bells, handkerchiefs and sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris belonged to the Pre-Raphaelite set, and the same surname names a traditional English folk dance.

clue.text: Novelist in audio reproduction

indicators.note: a reproduction is a remade version, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist is heard in a sound recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audio reproduction' looks like hi-fi talk; the second word acts on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouida was the pen name of Maria Louise Ramé, a Victorian writer of popular romances.

clue.text: In railway express what one may feel in a detached way

indicators.note: one thing in another is set inside it

blocks.note: RLY is the standard abbreviation for railway
to emote is to display one's feelings

explanation.surface: Describing how a passenger on an express train might feel aloof from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railway express' looks like a train, but 'express' starts the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting distantly or aloofly, from far off, is behaving in a detached manner.

clue.text: Prepares at last to strip off skimpy garment

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: last letter of prepares
to strip off is to take one's clothes off

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets ready to take off a revealing piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, low-cut summer frock leaving arms and shoulders bare is a scanty item of clothing.

clue.text: Float fitted with alarm— you'll be blamed initially for getting jittery

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
something jittery is shaking about, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
first letter of blamed

explanation.surface: A warning that you will take the blame when an alarm-fitted float starts rattling about.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'Float fitted with alarm' look like a heading for what follows, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker floating at sea that carries a bell, rung by the waves to warn shipping, matches a float with an alarm.

clue.text: Immutable— an edict from sultan

blocks.note: firm means fixed, not to be changed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sultan's decree is declared unchangeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A firman was a decree or grant issued by an Eastern ruler, especially the Ottoman sultan.

clue.text: During school, one child is kept in over break

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the short word is read backwards
kept in means held inside, like a pupil in detention

blocks.note: in means during
a school term is the session pupils attend
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil is given detention during term, held in over the break.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics in the printed clue hint at a whole story about school detention; 'is' is a piece of wordplay, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval between parts of a play or film is a pause, the noun sense of a rest period.

clue.text: Allowed boy to go on stage

indicators.note: one part going on another means it is placed after it

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
Al is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy is given permission to go on stage as an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests the theatre, but here it is a section of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by law or by the rules is allowed, the adjective sense of the word.

clue.text: After repair, send car to town

indicators.note: a repair puts parts back together in a different working order, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once it has been mended, a car is to be dispatched to some town.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is a town in South Yorkshire, England, famous for its racecourse.

clue.text: Recommend an astrological influence to decide the issue

blocks.note: to tip something is to recommend it
the Scales is Libra, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone suggests consulting the stars to settle a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To be the factor that settles a balanced contest is an idiom drawn from a weighing balance.

clue.text: Governor of castle can't be so careless about money

indicators.note: something careless is done sloppily, so the letters fall out of order
about means around, so the jumble goes round another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The keeper of a castle must not be so careless with its finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the warden or keeper appointed to command a royal castle held this title.

clue.text: One working as hooker on the staff — black mark

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for a small hook, from French for little hook
second meaning: a musical note written as a filled-in black head on the stave

explanation.surface: A worker on the payroll who acts as a prostitute earns a black mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' and 'staff' suggest an employee scandal; the staff is the five lines of written music, and the note's name comes from the word for a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: The quarter note has a solid black head on the stave, and the word originally meant a small hook.

clue.text: Go off top of hill to highway

blocks.note: milk that goes off turns sour
a pike is a peaked hilltop, as in Lake District names like Scafell Pike

explanation.surface: Directions to leave the summit and head for the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike was a main road with tollgates, and in America the word still means a toll motorway.

clue.text: One with unexpectedly good heart announced he'd trump another suit

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: he would ruff, that is, play a trump in a card game; the pronoun is surface
diamonds is a suit of cards

explanation.surface: At bridge, someone with a surprisingly good hand of hearts declares they will trump another suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all card play: 'heart' and 'suit' pretend to be bridge terms, but hearts belong to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with coarse manners but a kind nature underneath, like an uncut gem, has an unexpectedly good heart.

clue.text: Violently expel air from tin — simplicity itself, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is taken by how it is said

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ease is simplicity

explanation.surface: Blowing air out of a tin can is said to be the simplest thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary burst of breath through nose and mouth is a violent expulsion of air, the verb sense.

clue.text: What expensive boat cost?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about the price of a pricey vessel
setter's reading: the word names a kind of mail boat and is also slang for a large sum, so the boat cost itself

explanation.walkthrough: A packet boat carried mail and passengers on a regular route; 'cost a packet' is British slang for being very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scheduled mail ship and, informally, a large amount of money.

clue.text: Note in miniaturised state gives thin metallic sound

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: the state of being very small
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A musical note played by something tiny comes out sounding thin and metallic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that is thin and metallic is like a tin can rattling, the noun quality described.

clue.text: Hindu god of wind, rain, etc

definitions.text: Hindu god of wind, rain, etc

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A plain encyclopedia entry for the Hindu deity of the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: With no indicator, the whole clue is both the definition and the place where the answer is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Vedic religion the king of the gods rules the sky, sending thunder, rain and storms.

clue.text: Fly from island kingdom

blocks.note: first meaning: a fly is a light horse carriage
second meaning: the Polynesian kingdom in the South Pacific

explanation.surface: Someone flies out of a South Sea island kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb, but it is the old noun for a horse-drawn hired carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a South Pacific island monarchy, and the same word names a light Indian horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: First in, Hobbs had the style to perform the cut ...

indicators.note: first in asks for the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: first letter of Hobbs
an air is a manner or style
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Jack Hobbs, opening the batting, had the style to play the cut shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Hobbs was a great English opening batsman, and the cut is a cricket stroke, so the surface is pure cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut styled in a particular way is a cut, so the hairstyle is the barber's result.

clue.text: ..to secure a quick run that may decide the match

blocks.note: to tie is to fasten or secure
a break is a dash or quick run, as in breaking for cover

explanation.surface: Continuing the cricket scene: a batsman snatching a quick run that could win the match.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an extra game is played to settle a deadlocked set, and so can settle the contest.

clue.text: Greek musicians stopped short

indicators.note: stopping short means not reaching the end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a group of musicians is the band

explanation.surface: A group of Greek musicians stopped playing abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Thebes, the ancient city in Boeotia, is a Greek.

clue.text: Wearing respectable blue

blocks.note: you are in the clothes you are wearing
decent means respectable

explanation.surface: Someone is dressed in a respectable shade of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'decent' also means being dressed, which makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are smutty or obscene, a common informal sense of the colour word.
